name: Chitosan: Nature's Armor Turned Medical Marvel
notation_note: Chitosan is chitin with most of its acetyl groups removed; the degree of deacetylation varies by preparation, so real material is a copolymer of the unit shown and the acetylated chitin unit.
historical_events_referenced: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space (1961)

historical_images.alt: A uniformed man standing in an open-topped car decorated with flowers, waving to a dense crowd lining a tree-lined avenue, with police motorcyclists riding alongside.
historical_images.caption: Yuri Gagarin touring Warsaw in 1961, the year materials science's postwar boom gave way to a more deliberate, engineering-driven era.

historical_images.caption: Charles Rouget, who first deacetylated chitin into a soluble derivative in 1859 and called it 'chitine modifiée.'

historical_images.caption: Felix Hoppe-Seyler, who gave Rouget's modified chitin the name chitosan in 1894.

historical_images.alt: A dense pile of small pink and translucent whole shrimp, seen from directly above, filling the entire frame.
historical_images.caption: Raw material rather than raw curiosity: chitosan begins as the shell of a shrimp or crab, most of which the seafood industry would otherwise throw away.

density.conditions: 20 °C, solid; bulk (powder) density is much lower, 0.4-0.68 g/cm³.

water_absorption.conditions: moisture absorption, equilibrium at 23 °C/50% RH (not immersion)

synthesis.industrial_process_notes: Chitin was first isolated in 1799 by Charles Hatchett; deacetylated chitin was named 'chitosan' in 1894 by Felix Hoppe-Seyler. Commercial production deacetylates chitin using excess sodium hydroxide in water, giving average molecular weights of 3,800-20,000 Da. Renewed research interest emerged in the 1970s driven by shellfish-waste disposal regulations.

structure_morphology.crystal_structure: Orthorhombic unit cell (a = 0.895 nm, b = 1.697 nm, c = 1.037 nm), 4 chains per unit cell with 8 associated water molecules; chains adopt a 2-fold helix conformation.
structure_morphology.chain_flexibility_notes: Degree of deacetylation (65-95%, commonly ~90% in commercial grades) governs solubility and reactivity.

mw.conditions: Spans low-Mw (20,000-190,000) and high-Mw (190,000-375,000) commercial grades; a representative Mw of 150,000 is also cited.

tensile_strength_at_break.conditions: Wide range reflects different film-casting/plasticizer conditions; amorphous film, no distinct yield point.

acids.conditions: dilute and concentrated; soluble below pH 6 (forms soluble salts with organic acid anions) -- acetic acid, formic acid and concentrated mineral acids are listed as good solvents

hydrolysis_resistance.value: moderate -- susceptible to lysozyme and specific glycosidase hydrolysis
hydrolysis_resistance.conditions: Enzymes hydrolyzing glucosamine-glucosamine and N-acetylglucosamine-N-acetylglucosamine linkages degrade chitosan; also degraded by lysozyme.

environmental.degradation_pathway: Enzymatic hydrolysis (chitosanase, lysozyme) of glycosidic linkages; biodegradable.
environmental.environmental_notes: Commercial production valorizes shellfish-processing waste. Low aquatic toxicity reported: 100% survival in 48 h tests on Daphnia magna, fathead minnow and rainbow trout; rainbow trout LC50 >10,000 mg/l.

structure_render_2d.alt: Repeat unit of Chitosan, drawn as a skeletal structure with polymer brackets
structure_render_2d.author: Atlas of Polymers

structure_render_3d.alt: Ball-and-stick model of one Chitosan repeat unit
structure_render_3d.caption: A three-unit model is available alongside this one.
structure_render_3d.author: Atlas of Polymers

ld50_oral_rat.conditions: Reported for oral mouse (source's own designation), not rat; >16,000 mg/kg (practically non-toxic).

carcinogenic_classification.value: not listed by ACGIH, NIOSH, NTP
